appraisal_events.evidence: Je ne devais plus cesser... d'être continuellement invité... amis auxquels ils me présentaient avec une nuance de bienveillance si marquée... qu'il n'est pas un d'entre eux qui n'eût cru manquer au duc et à la duchesse s'il avait donné un bal sans me faire figurer sur sa liste.
appraisal_events.explanation: The Guermantes' intimate circle treats the narrator as a favored, indispensable guest, marking a real rise in his social standing, though this sits inside a mock-ritual, faintly ironic frame ('Cène sociale').

appraisal_events.evidence: ce fut par la véritable méchanceté de Mme de Guermantes que je fus révolté quand, la princesse de Parme ayant timidement proposé d'en parler d'elle-même... la duchesse fit tout ce qu'elle put pour en détourner l'Altesse. — Mais Madame... Monserfeuil n'a aucune espèce de crédit ni de pouvoir avec le nouveau gouvernement.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly names the duchesse's conduct as genuine unkindness for discouraging the princesse de Parme from helping her nephew Robert, whose post is dangerous, exposing calculated cruelty behind a plausible-sounding excuse.

status_effects.explanation: He becomes a habitual, favored guest whose absence from any Guermantes-adjacent invitation list would seem an affront, marking real elevation within this circle.
He is folded into the intimate, ritualized inner circle of the household's closest friends rather than remaining an occasional outside guest.
The narrator directly condemns her as genuinely unkind for blocking help to her endangered nephew behind a flimsy pretext about the general's lack of influence.
Her timid attempt to intervene for Robert is deflected by the duchesse, and she is reduced to murmuring more quietly rather than pressing her point, despite her higher rank.
His aunt's refusal to use her influence leaves his dangerous posting unaddressed despite the princesse de Parme's willingness to intervene on his behalf.

ambiguities: The referent of 'la princesse' throughout is resolved as princesse de Parme based on the later explicit mention 'la princesse de Parme' discussing the same Monserfeuil/Robert topic, though the opening exchange alone does not name her explicitly.

The mock-religious imagery describing the Guermantes' hospitality ('Cène sociale', 'apôtres de la Sainte-Chapelle') is faintly ironic, which qualifies but does not clearly negate the narrator's own elevation within that circle.
